title: Bengals nearly made a costly trade-deadline blunder, and Zac Taylor had to explain it - CBS Sports

body:
The Bengals agreed to acquire Ebiketie from the Eagles before discovering the deal could cost them way more than they thought
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There were six trades on trade deadline day Tuesday, but a trade that didn't happen provided one of the more entertaining moments of what was already a wild day.The Bengals agreed to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles for edge defender Arnold Ebiketie, a fairly run-of-the-mill deal on the surface: Ebiketie figured to join the Bengals' pass-rush rotation with Cashius Howell (wrist) on IR. But it seemed the Bengals failed to realize or understand that the trade would have meant also forfeiting the compensatory 2027 third-round pick they are due after losing Trey Hendrickson in free agency.The trade fell through after the Bengals, it seems, learned about that part of the equation. Wednesday, Bengals coach Zac Taylor addressed the near-trade."I feel good (about the EDGE depth)," Taylor said. "Obviously we tried something yesterday, and [director of personnel] Duke [Tobin] was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed, and I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked. 
"We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our, and that's just the way things go, but certainly have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things, and they've given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now and playing at such a high level. So, we'll put that behind us and move forward ..."Nick Korte, who contributes to the contract source site OverTheCap, was first to point the potential snafu out. The Eagles signed Ebiketie as a compensatory free agent this offseason, meaning he counted against the compensatory pick formula. That status carries over if he is traded in-season, per the Collective Bargaining Agreement. Here's the full chart:
The Bengals may have believed Cordell Volson counted as a CFA lost, but he has not played this year, rendering his departure moot in the compensatory picks balance.

        
            
                Bengals call off Arnold Ebiketie trade with Eagles after nearly botching compensatory pick situation
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
To his credit, Taylor said the failed trade didn't interrupt his Tuesday preparation, aside from the very brief conversation he had with Tobin, and that it would not impact the team's preparation for a crucial Week 10 "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Steelers. Cincinnati and Pittsburgh are tied for the AFC North lead at 6-2.The Bengals ended up not making any in-season trades this year, even while most other top AFC teams, including the Jaguars, Chiefs and Broncos, did. Taylor had a lot of confidence in the group he has, which has won four straight."I really like where we're at," Taylor said. "I think Duke really likes where we're at. So this is a team with a lot of confidence right now. I know it's a fun period of time, the weeks leading up to the trade deadline, for fans and people to generate a lot of media attention of of it, but the truth is we really do like where we're at."

        New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler is the winner of the American League Cy Young Award for 2026. Schlittler was a unanimous selection via the Baseball Writers Association of America balloting, the results of which were announced on Wednesday, beating out Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease and Guardians rookie Parker Messick. Schlittler's win snapped the run of free agent Tarik Skubal, who won the last two AL Cy Youngs as a member of the Detroit Tigers.  This past season, the right-handed Schlitter in his age-25 campaign put up dominant numbers:  
In addition to the above, Schlitter led AL pitchers in WAR with a mark of 7.0, and his ERA+ of 215 also paced his league. That 215 ERA+, which means that Schlittler's park-adjusted ERA was 115% better than the league average, is a Yankees franchise record. Among Yankee qualifiers, only Ron Guidry's 208 in 1978 comes close. Additionally, Schlittler tied for the AL lead this season with an FIP of 2.56, and he struck out 31.4% of opposing batters, which also ranked second in the AL.  Without Schlittler's top-shelf contributions, the Yankees, without franchise slugger and reigning back-to-back AL MVP Aaron Judge for almost 100 games, might have struggled to make the postseason. Instead, Schlittler's excellence at the front of the rotation helped them win 93 games, post the AL's top run differential, and advance to the ALDS.
"Cam had as dominant a season as a starting pitcher can have from start to finish," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said in a statement. "He's shown an astonishing amount of growth since we drafted him, and his success is no accident. Cam has a tireless appetite for hard work and refinement that has allowed his talents to truly flourish. This Cy Young is richly deserved. Cam was the most dominant pitcher in our league and continues to grow into a foundational player for this franchise."Here are the voting totals: 				1st place				2nd place				3rd place				4th place5th placePointsCam Schlittler, Yankees30				 				 				 				 210Dylan Cease, Blue Jays				 2262				 110Parker Messick, Guardians				 7129284Drew Rasmussen, Rays				 11215272Sonny Gray, Red Sox				 				 				 31521Reid Detmers, Angels				 				 				 179Cade Smith, Guardians				 				 				 				 22Bryan Baker, Rays				 				 				 				 11Michael Wacha, Royals				 				 				 				 11While Schlittler was outstanding as a rookie in 2025, this past season, he increased usage of his sinker and cutter and improved ride on his 98-mph fastball helped him take the next step and become one of the very pitchers in all of baseball.         San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award. The BBWAA introduced the award this year and, moving forward, will hand it out annually along with Rookies and Managers of the Year, Cy Young, and MVPs.   The BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively. The Rivera and Hoffman Awards replaced the Delivery Man of the Year Award in 2015 and are voted on by a panel of former relievers, including Rivera and Hoffman.    Like the other BBWAA awards, the new Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       National League: Mason Miller, Padres   The best closer in baseball is the first-ever BBWAA National League Reliever of the Year. Miller was overwhelming from start to finish this past season, pitching to a 1.67 ERA with 129 strikeouts in only 70 innings. He led all pitchers with 3.9 WAR, well ahead of second-place Louie Varland (3.1 WAR), and he led the NL in saves (38) and games finished (57).

He was acquired from the Athletics at the 2025 trade deadline at a very high cost: San Diego sent shortstop Leo De Vries, one of the best prospects in baseball, to the A's in the six-player deal. Miller has been worth the price, though. He owns a 1.45 ERA in parts of two seasons with the Padres.   This is the first major award of Miller's career, who finished fourth in the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year voting and has two All-Star Game selections (2024 and 2026), but otherwise had never received Cy Young or MVP votes prior to this season. He beat out the Brewers' Trevor Megill and Phillies' Jhoan Duran for the award.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
       American League: Louis Varland, Blue Jays   After jumping into the national spotlight with his high usage during the 2025 postseason, Varland is the first winner of the BBWAA American League Reliever of the Year award. His 1.27 ERA led qualified relievers and his 3.1 WAR was tops in the AL. Varland struck out 87 batters in 78 innings and was fifth with 35 saves. Breaking down which early-season struggles warrant real concern and which emerging waiver targets have earned sustainable roles

        Not every fantasy basketball breakout comes from a lottery pick or a household name. From Davion Mitchell and Ajay Mitchell to Kyshawn George and Rui Hachimura, several players are seizing bigger roles, new opportunities and expanded workloads to post career-best numbers. Before you dismiss a hot start as a small-sample fluke, you need to know which surges are built to last and which are tied to temporary injury openings. We break down 15 fantasy basketball players taking their game to a new level, including Dyson Daniels, Ayo Dosunmu, Anthony Black and Naz Reid, and explain what's driving each one's rise. Here is who deserves a spot on your fantasy radar as the 2026-27 season unfolds.Rui Hachimura, Clippers Hachimura did well in a starting role with the Lakers over the past three seasons, but he is benefiting from a step up in the offensive hierarchy with his new squad, averaging the second-most shots per game (13.3) on the team. Through seven games, he is averaging a career-high 14.4 points, along with 5.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists and a career-best 1.1 steals.  Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Hawks Alexander-Walker took a major leap last season, earning himself the Most Improved Player award. He has kept the momentum going early this season, pushing for new career highs in points, three-pointers made and steals per game. With a firm hold on the starting role, he is likely to reach new heights in one or more areas of his game.  Dyson Daniels, Hawks Daniels has been arguably the most important player for his squad this season, making a massive impact with his defensive skill set, including a whopping 3.0 steals per game, which ties his career high set in 2024-25. He also averages 9.8 points on 48.1 percent shooting, a career-high 7.1 rebounds and 5.8 assists in 30.3 minutes per outing.
Aaron Wiggins, Hawks Wiggins has been a great addition for the Hawks, as he is showing improvement across the board, averaging 14.9 points per game this season, up from 9.4 last season, while playing just an additional 4 minutes per game. He is also knocking down a career-best 3.0 threes per game on 41.9 percent shooting from deep. Davion Mitchell, Heat Mitchell has been showing good improvement over the last couple of seasons but is vaulting into some new conversations, averaging 16.5 points on 49.6 percent shooting, 2.0 rebounds, 8.5 assists (fourth-most in the league) and 1.3 steals through 11 games. At the current rate, the 28-year-old is playing like one of the better-producing point guards out there, and he is likely to continue thriving alongside Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo.Naz Reid, Hornets Reid opened the season with a 20-point, 11-rebound, seven-assist showing and averaged 19.5 points, 9.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists through his first four games. He slowed down a bit over the next few outings but picked it up again by reaching the 25-point mark twice in the last three games. He also has four double-doubles this season. The big man is likely to keep stuffing the stat sheet in an expanded role with his new squad. 
Anthony Black, Magic Black got the opportunity to show what he can do in extended minutes while covering for injuries last season, and the situation has arisen early again this year. The fourth-year guard is averaging career highs across the board through seven games, with 17.1 points, 5.9 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.0 steals. With great size for the position and the ability to score at three levels, he should continue to stand out as a high-level producer even if he returns to a bench role.   Daniss Jenkins, Pistons Jenkins is off to a great start and making a case for himself as a key piece to the Pistons' identity. He is averaging 12.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and 4.7 assists in 26.0 minutes per game, all of which stand as career-high marks. He is also coming off two great games, with a 31-point outing, which helped earn him the start in the most recent game, where he turned in 22 points, six rebounds, eight assists and a season-high four steals.Paul Reed, Pistons Reed showed some great flashes last season, notably when he had the chance to step into a bigger role to cover injuries. He's had that opportunity again early this season, as Jalen Duren has been out for the last couple of weeks, and Reed has shined once again, averaging 11.1 points, 7.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks in 27.1 minutes per game over that span. He could see a bit of a reduced role when Duren returns but is likely to continue making an impact even off the bench. 
Jamal Shead, Raptors  Shead opened the season with at least five assists in seven of his first eight games, while averaging 21.5 minutes per outing. He then put everyone on notice by dropping back-to-back points-and-assists double-doubles in the last two outings, when he has had the chance to start due to injuries in the lineup. The third-year guard surely has some untapped potential that should result in a continued rise in production, even out of a backup role. Ja'Kobe Walter, Raptors Walter demonstrated the ability to contribute as a solid rotation player over his first two seasons and continues to make progress in his third season, especially thanks to the opportunity to step up in the absence of Kawhi Leonard. Walter is slowly carving out a reputation as a three-and-D archetype, averaging 1.2 steals and 2.1 made three-pointers in 29.6 minutes per game this year. Ajay Mitchell, Thunder Mitchell showed some flashes last season, which likely gave the Thunder leadership confidence to part ways with guys like Aaron Wiggins, Isaiah Joe and Luguentz Dort in the offseason. Mitchell has carried over the strong play and is making the most of the boost in responsibility by averaging 18.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.2 steals while shooting an impressive 52.3 percent from the field. He is in line to keep up a heavy workload due to the absences of Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams for most of the season. 
Ayo Dosunmu, Timberwolves Dosunmu has deserved a larger role over the past couple of seasons and is getting the chance as a result of Anthony Edwards' absence. Dosunmu is averaging 18.1 points, 4.9 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.3 steals in 31.4 minutes per game, proving himself as a legitimate stat-sheet stuffer. Brandin Podziemski, Warriors Podziemski has been working to fill a big void for the Warriors over the last couple of seasons and has done a fair job. However, he has looked more confident lately, shooting an impressive 48.2 percent from the field, including 40.3 percent from deep, and limiting himself to 1.3 turnovers per game. He also continues to chip in on defense, averaging 1.2 steals per game. Kyshawn George, Wizards George showed some brilliant flashes through his first couple of seasons and seems to be bringing it all together in his third season, averaging 17.9 points on 48.7 percent shooting, 4.4 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 1.4 blocks in 33.2 minutes per game. At 6-foot-8 and with a good motor, the 22-year-old is emerging as a bona fide menace for opponents.

title: Dan Lanning fires back at Michigan's Kyle Whittingham over NIL criticism - CBS Sports
description: The Oregon coach provided his own spicy soundbite ahead of Saturday's game with Michigan
body:
The Oregon coach provided his own spicy soundbite ahead of Saturday's game with Michigan

                •

        The postgame handshake between Dan Lanning and Kyle Whittingham will be something to monitor on Saturday as Michigan matches up against No. 16 Oregon in Eugene. That's because -- as politely as possible -- Lanning and Whittingham have exchanged barbs about each program's NIL spending.Two days after Whittingham accused Lanning and Oregon of simply outbidding teams for players, Lanning got his opportunity to respond. During his Wednesday press conference, Lanning said the Wolverines might be more competitive on the NIL market if they weren't spending so much money on fired coaches and signing the wrong players to big deals."I've got nothing to say to Coach Whitt other than I think he's an unbelievable coach," Lanning said. "I get it. They're spending more of their money now on coaches they're letting go. Maybe it makes it hard to sign players."They've signed a couple of guys with what weren't able to compete with what they decided to do. Maybe a lot of that is tied up in another player, but I don't know. Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He's a Hall of Fame coach. I've got nothing but respect for him."
With Michigan scoring 19.6 points per game, the team just fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck and paid him a jaw-dropping $10.2 million buyout.On a related note, sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood was benched in favor of freshman Tommy Carr, as Underwood regressed under a new offensive scheme. Underwood, the No. 1 player in the 2025 signing class, was paid handsomely by the Wolverines.Not to put words in Lanning's mouth, but it would be easy to draw a line from his comments about Michigan having a lot of money tied up in "another player" to Underwood.

        
            
                A three-loss team is getting into the CFP, but which contender holds the inside track?
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Whittingham began the pot-stirringIn fairness to Lanning, he did bookend his answer with praise for Whittingham, even if there was a series of thinly-veiled insults in the middle. He may have taken that page right out of Whittingham's playbook after the Michigan coach complimented Lanning's recruiting prowess before talking about Oregon's NIL budget."(Lanning's an) outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach; that's his background, but tireless recruiter," Whittingham said. "He really does a great job recruiting. It doesn't hurt that you have $50 million at your disposal to, in essence, to outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that's not his fault. That's a credit. I mean, that's a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have."Oregon does have one of the most expensive rosters in college football this season, but Michigan can't exactly cry poor either. The Wolverines are spending more than $30 million on their football team this fall.
To this point, neither team has gotten a great return on that investment. The Wolverines have been eliminated from College Football Playoff contention, and the Ducks are one loss away from missing out too.

title: Stephen Curry fires back at critics of wife Ayesha's on-screen kiss in acting role - CBS Sports
description: Ayesha Curry's acting performance has drawn plenty of attention on the ex-NBA player podcast circuit
body:
Ayesha Curry's acting performance has drawn plenty of attention on the ex-NBA player podcast circuit
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Roku Channel's new Christmas movie, Second Chance Holiday, premiered last Thursday, starring an actress in her first leading role: Ayesha Curry. The wife of Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has 20 acting credits on IMDB, but has never headlined a movie before, and with that new stature has come criticism.On the "We Said What We Said" podcast, former NBA players Gilbert Arenas and Nick Young took issue with Curry kissing co-star Matthew Daddario. "The only blemish in the family is the wife, in a sense," Arenas said. "Because she doesn't act like the other superstars' wives. You know, Jordan's wife; Cookie, that's Magic's wife; Savannah, right, where we don't want to hear you. We just want to know you're there. You're fine. You're taking the pictures, but we don't want to know you." Arenas claimed that Curry speaks to other men via direct messages on social media because "she needs the attention because he doesn't give her the attention because he's focused," alluding to previous comments Curry made about having "zero male attention."Former NFL running back LeSean McCoy also cited that conversation in criticizing Curry. "This is crazy. You got one of the greatest players of all time as your husband," McCoy said on Speakeasy. "I've seen a while ago where she keeps saying how she wants more attention, and how girls throw themselves at him and she still just wants to feel like she's wanted… now you want us to see kissing a dude?… This is crazy."On Wednesday, Stephen Curry addressed the comments with a video on Instagram.


"Nick, Gil, Emmanuel and anybody else who feels the need to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about, something that kind of speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do," Curry said. "Given the ignorance around how acting works, obviously I tried to laugh this one off but something needs to be said. Anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, kindly suggest that you just give the happy hands, the congratulations, and maybe the apology can be as loud as when y'all leading y'all shows with this topic."Both Young, a former teammate of Curry's with the Warriors, and Arenas apologized Wednesday. "You my dog. I love you. If I said anything, I apologize like a man. I'm sorry," Young said. "I'm sorry if he's offended; I didn't mean it like that. I was just saying, he's such a perfect dude," Arenas added, saying that Curry had never drawn controversy himself, but if someone in the family had, it was Ayesha.NBA superstars are used to negativity from pundits, but commentary about their family is another matter. What Ayesha Curry does as an actress in a movie says nothing about her family or her husband's place in the basketball world. It's rare that Stephen Curry would address comments like this, but aside from the offense he and his family took, he was at least able to use it as a promotional opportunity. 
"Appreciate the free pub, thank you for giving a nice shout-out to Second Chance Holiday," he said at the end of his video.

        Three teams have revamped their receiving corps heading into Week 10 because of injuries or trades. The Rams are without Puka Nacua (knee), the Cardinals don't have Michael Wilson (neck), and the Colts traded Keenan Allen to San Francisco and Josh Downs to Kansas City.It's messy what was left behind on those rosters, and none of the receivers for the Rams, Cardinals or Colts are worth starting in most Fantasy leagues. But we do have some potential sleepers in deeper formats.Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield are both worth a look with their matchup at Arizona in Week 10. Nacua missed two games earlier this season with a hip injury while Davante Adams (hamstring) was still healthy, and Mumpfield had a huge game in Week 3 at Denver with four catches for 93 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. And in 2024, before Adams was with the Rams, Nacua missed five games with a knee injury, and Atwell scored at least 11.1 PPR points in four of those outings and averaged 6.8 targets per game over that span. 
I prefer Atwell over Mumpfield if you have to decide between the two, but neither one is anything more than a low-end starter in three-receiver leagues. Most likely, the Rams will lean on their running backs and tight ends before any of their receivers.With Wilson out, the Cardinals' top three receivers are Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay. None of them are worth using in most formats, especially with Carson Beck making his first NFL start against the Rams. The only pass catcher I would use for Arizona is Trey McBride.
For the Colts, I would only trust Tyler Warren in Week 10 against Miami, and we'll see how they use Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Ashton Dulin and Anthony Gould. Given how poorly Daniel Jones has done this year in connecting with Allen and Downs, it's unlikely any of the new Indianapolis receivers will play well enough to help Fantasy managers aside from the deepest of leagues.

body:
Saves or ERA? Does workload matter? How Matt Snyder voted in the first-ever BBWAA Reliever of the Year award
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mason Miller of the Padres won the 2026 National League Reliever of the Year award on Wednesday evening. That wasn't all too surprising, but I still wanted to explain the thought process behind my ballot. This was an honor, as it was the first-ever Baseball Writers' Association of America award for a relief pitcher. Yes, there have been plenty of reliever awards over the years, but this was the first year the BBWAA handed out such hardware.My ballot for this one: 1. Mason Miller, Padres2. Jhoan Duran, Phillies3. Adrián Morejón, Padres4. Trevor Megill, Brewers5. Mason Montgomery, PiratesAnd now here's how it unfolded on my end. First off, I didn't even bother to look at win-loss record. It's a flawed enough stat these days with any individual player, but we really shouldn't be judging relievers by it. I'm also not worried about team performance here, as this is an individual award and we don't even need to wrestle with the word "valuable" being in the title like some MVP voters might. This is simply, "Who was the best relief pitcher in the league?" 
        
            
                Padres' Mason Miller, Blue Jays' Louis Varland named MLB Relievers of the Year in first-ever BBWAA award
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
What makes the best relievers? Run prevention (ERA, FIP, xFIP, etc.) matters, as does keeping runners off base (WHIP). It's helpful not only to the defense to strike hitters out, but it can also help a reliever bail out his team, so that's going to matter. Workload matters as well, as a reliever eating up as many outs as possible is very valuable to a team. I didn't factor saves as much as keeping leads (blown saves can hurt). Something I find helpful in judging relievers is win probability added. A reliever blowing games is going to be dinged in a big way, while closing down tougher games (one-run leads as opposed to three) is going to score extra via this measure. It's trickier with relievers, but WAR can help tell a story here, too. 
Finally, I have no doubt there was some eye test involved. That is, when I'm watching a game, which reliever coming out of the bullpen feels the most imposing to the opposition. Miller, Duran and Megill especially got bonus points here. A quick rundown of the major stats I examined follows. Run prevention and keeping guys off baseAmong NL relievers, Miller was the best in ERA (1.67), xERA, FIP, xFIP and several other categories. Duran was second in ERA (and xERA, FIP and xFIP) with Yuki Matsui third, Brandyn Garcia fourth and Abner Uribe fifth. Megill was third in FIP, while Montgomery was third in xFIP and Morejón was fourth. In terms of keeping runners off base, Garcia led NL relievers in WHIP; Megill was second, Miller third, Duran ninth and Montgomery 10th. 
Kudos to Garcia for the excellent season, but his workload (51 ⅓ innings) dinged him a bit. Speaking of, Morejón worked 86 innings compared to 70 from Miller, 63 ⅔ from Montgomery, 61 ⅔ from Megill and 59 ⅓ from Duran. That said, Garcia, Matsui and Uribe are firmly in the mix through these categories. Missing batsMiller crushes here. He struck out 129 hitters, giving him 16.6 K/9 and a 47.4 K%. Montgomery was second in strikeout rate at 37.7%. Yes, it was that much of a blowout for Miller. Duran was third at 35.6%. Garcia was sixth, Morejón ninth, Megill 14th, Uribe 25th and Matsui 28th. 
Holding leadsMiller tied for the league lead in saves with Riley O'Brien. I never considered O'Brien, as his ERA was north of 4.00. Miller was also 38 of 41 in save chances. Duran was 33 of 35. Megill had 30 saves and seven holds with only three blown saves. Montgomery had 18 saves and nine holds with three blown saves. Morejón blew five saves, but he had three saves and 28 holds with an awful lot of multi-inning appearances. Uribe had six saves and 23 holds with two blown saves. Garcia? Stellar. He closed down five saves and 18 holds without ever blowing a lead. Matsui never blew a lead either, but he only had one save and 10 holds, meaning he wasn't tasked with much in the way of high-leverage innings. Being teammates with Miller and Morejón (and Jasaon Adam and Bradgley Rodríguez) will do that. As such, along with his relatively low strikeout rate, we can safely eliminate Matsui. By the time I've gotten here, I have seven players for five spots: Miller, Morejón, Duran, Megill, Montgomery, Uribe and Garcia.
WPA/WARLet's start with WAR. Using the FanGraphs calculation, Miller leads the way by a country mile at 3.7. Duran is second at 2.9, with Morejón at 2.8 and Megill at 2.5. Montgomery is eighth, Uribe ninth and Garcia, due in part to the workload concern, down at 17th. Over on Baseball Reference's version, Duran actually leads the way at 3.4. Miller is next at 3.1, followed by Montgomery (2.4) and Uribe (2.3). Megill sits at 1.7 while both Morejón and Garcia are at 1.9. In WPA, yes, Miller leads the way again at 4.56. Uribe is second at 3.49, with Morejón third at 3.23, Montgomery fourth at 2.86, Megill seventh, Garcia eighth and Duran 11th. 
Miller in first place wasn't all too difficult. He was the best relief pitcher in baseball in 2026 and checked every single box. I had trouble with Duran over Morejón, while Megill and Montgomery were also very close in that group, as were Uribe and Garcia. I ended up leaning on Duran's high strikeout rate and excellent run prevention, which helped clear the way for his lead in WAR. Morejón's workload meant I couldn't go any lower than third with him, given how many important outs he soaked up for the Padres. Megill's regular-season numbers were better than Uribe's, notably the under-the-hood numbers, even if they were very close. And Montgomery was an absolute beast for the Pirates. It was incredibly tough to leave Uribe off, and Garcia was my hard-luck seventh-place finisher here when I had only five spots on my ballot.

Gardner Minshew's season-ending injury opens the door for Beck, whose first assignment comes against one of the NFL's most accomplished pass-rushing duos

        If the 2026 NFL season feels like an unprecedented year for unheralded rookie quarterbacks, that's because it is. With the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) announcing Carson Beck as their starting quarterback for Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams (5-4), he will now be the third rookie quarterback drafted outside of the first two rounds to start a game this season. The other two were undrafted rookies -- Jalon Daniels of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Joe Fagnano of the Baltimore Ravens. That hasn't happened since 1987."You never really know until you get to the live bullets on Sunday, but just the way he goes about his business, whether it's been from OTAs through training camp before he got hurt, seeing him operate in that first half," coach Mike LaFleur said. "Plus, the one possession there in the second half, so obviously we'll know more come next Sunday, but we have all the confidence he's ready to roll."In the Hall of Fame game that kicked off the 2026 preseason, Beck completed 15 of his 19 throws for 188 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers. Beck will also become the fifth quarterback to make his first career start against a duo of pass rushers with 100-plus sacks each when he faces the Rams' duo of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. 
"Who do they got?" LaFleur said jokingly. "I got no expectations for him except to go out and play his game one play at a time. Go let it rip, go have some fun. Have some fun with your guys."A depleted group represents Beck's supporting cast, with Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) out for the season and Marvin Harrison Jr. traded to the Houston Texans. Fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil, undrafted veteran Simi Fehoko and Pro Bowl return man Devin Duvernay are the projected starters. 
Fortunately, Beck also has the 2025 first-team All-Pro tight end at his disposal in Trey McBride. McBride leads the NFL with 73 catches through Week 9, and he has 11 consecutive games with at least seven catches. Beck also knows a thing or two about feeding his superstar tight end after his years teaming with Brock Bowers at Georgia.

title: College football transfer QB market faces severe shortage with top passers staying put - CBS Sports
description: With Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor finalizing a deal to become the latest high-profile quarterback to resign
body:
With Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor finalizing a deal to become the latest high-profile quarterback to resign with his team, the 2027 college football transfer QB pool is looking like a seller's market
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is set to become the latest quarterback to re-sign with his program on Wednesday as he finalizes a deal with the Bulldogs, multiple outlets report. With a contract expected to make him the highest-paid quarterback in the sport, Taylor's retention is a game-changing moment for the program. It's also yet another shot into the heart of the transfer portal quarterback class. Over the past several weeks, Missouri's Austin Simmons, Oregon State's Braden Atkinson and Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea have all reportedly signed deals to return to their programs. While plenty of contracts could be tested -- similar to Darian Mensah at Duke last season -- the number of portal targets is quickly declining. Out of the top 25 passers in college football, only 13 of them are listed as underclassmen. From that group, several are expected to either enter the NFL Draft early or return to their current schools, including Alabama's Keelon Russell and Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker. 
There's another group of quarterbacks who recently transferred into a program and might not want to start all over again. That includes names like Wake Forest's Gio Lopez, Baylor's DJ Lagway and Kentucky's Kenny Minchey. Unless something changes, the top quarterbacks on the board could be Memphis's Marcus Stokes, Texas State's Brad Jackson or NC State's CJ Bailey -- good players, but not ones ready to swing a national championship race. Complicating matters, there's a stunning number of teams hoping to find a program savior in the transfer portal. Texas A&M and Oklahoma view themselves as a quarterback away from returning to the playoff. Indiana and Miami have ridden transfers to the top. Even Oklahoma State and Notre Dame could look to the market if they lose passers to the NFL. 
Of course, there are a few wild cards in the mix. Texas quarterback Arch Manning has settled down in the second half of the year, but there were rumors he could explore his options. The same is true for Oregon's Dante Moore, who turned down being the No. 2 pick in the NFL Draft to return to school. After missing the second half of the season with a concussion, he might want a fresh start. Schools like LSU (Sam Leavitt) and Ohio State (Julian Sayin) will also have to make difficult decisions on quarterback contracts. But after looking to the market, they would be smart not to overthink things. Ready-made transfers have become a paradigm-shifting resource in the transfer portal era. Eight of the top 10 passers in the country are transfers, including each of the top three. But as even the developmental programs start turning to upperclassmen, the pipeline is rapidly drying up. 
Dozens of fanbases might soon head to the portal market in hopes of finding a program savior. There simply isn't the supply to meet the demand.

body:
The Giants needed a workhorse, the Rams needed a receiver and the Packers needed a running game, making these three missed deals natural fits
        
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        The 2026 trade deadline day didn't produce fireworks like last year, when the New York Jets dealt their best two defensive players in cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. The most consequential deadline day move was the Minnesota Vikings' reunion with Kirk Cousins, who was the team's quarterback from 2018 through 2023. The Vikings addressed a glaring need at quarterback by acquiring Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick. The Jacksonville Jaguars, who have a 6-2 record, went all in to win Super Bowl LXI by making aggressive moves a day earlier. Safety Jessie Bates III was acquired from the Atlanta Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Defensive tackle Jordan Davis was obtained from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. The Jaguars also traded a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the New Orleans Saints for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. Here are three more trades that should have been made before the deadline that may have improved teams' chances of making the postseason or going on a deep playoff run. The financial ramifications of the moves are highlighted. Salary cap space is based on NFLPA data. An acquiring team would have needed enough salary cap room to absorb the remainder of the player's current salary. Since the trades would have occurred after Week 9's games, the acquiring team would have been responsible for half of a player's 2026 base salary (9 of 18 total weeks) and any other applicable salary components in his contract. 
Trades can't be executed again until the 2027 league year begins on next March 11. Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor to New York Giants Giants get: Jonathan Taylor, 2028 sixth-round pickColts get: 2027 second-round pick, 2028 third-round pickTaylor Remaining 2026 Salary: $ 3.97 million Colts 2026 Salary Cap Savings: $4.60 million Giants 2026 Salary Cap Room: $6.18 millionColts 2027 Dead Money: $10 million ($11.02 million 2027 Salary Cap Savings)
The Colts went into fire sale mode after firing general manager Chris Ballard six games into the season. Criticism about the return when dealing perennial All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner may have contributed to the Colts holding firm on a steep asking price for Taylor. The Colts reportedly wanted a first-round pick or something comparable to the 2023 second, third, and fourth-round picks and the 2024 fifth-round pick the Carolina Panthers received from the San Francisco 49ers for All-Pro running back Christian McCaffrey during the 2022 season to part with Taylor.  That type of haul wasn't realistic. McCaffrey was 26 when he was dealt, while Taylor turns 28 in January. There's also a big discrepancy in mileage. Taylor's 1,712 career carries are almost double the 866 carries McCaffrey had with the Panthers prior to his trade. Taylor joined the exclusive $20-million-per-running-back club in August. He signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension (worth up to $47 million through incentives) with $39.02 million in guarantees and $23 million fully guaranteed at signing. Taylor's remaining 2026 compensation consists of $3.49 million in base salary and $480,000 of per-game active roster bonuses. Additionally, $625,000 of Taylor's $1 million in 2026 incentives is a salary cap charge because it is classified as likely to be earned, making a $4.595 million 2026 cap hit with him for the acquiring team. Taylor has two years worth $34 million remaining on his contract after this season. He is scheduled to make $16.02 million in 2027 and $17.98 million in 2028. 
The Colts could revisit a trade for Taylor during the offseason. It's likely that Taylor's trade value won't be any higher in the future.  The Giants reportedly were willing to give the Colts a second-round pick, a fifth-round pick, and an unnamed player for Taylor before pulling the offer. According to ESPN's Jordan Ranaan, the Giants called multiple teams about finding a workhorse running back as the trade deadline approached. Jacksonville Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. to Los Angeles RamsRams get: Brian Thomas Jr.Jaguars get: 2027 second-round pickRemaining 2026 Salary: $537,500 Jaguars 2026 Salary Cap Savings: $537,500Rams 2026 Salary Cap Room: $248,672Jaguars 2027 Dead Money: $1.8M ($2.8M Salary Cap Savings)
After his stellar 2024 rookie season in which he had 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns, Thomas has struggled ever since Liam Coen took over as Jaguars head coach. The 2024 first-round pick has become an afterthought in Jacksonville's passing game. Week 9's game against the Baltimore Ravens was the first time in Thomas' NFL career he wasn't targeted at least once. Thomas has 10 receptions, 117 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in eight games this season. Josh Cameron, a 2026 sixth-round pick, has more offensive snaps than Thomas since Week 4.  The Jaguars, who are in win-now mode, rebuffed trade interest in Thomas despite his dwindling role. Moving Thomas would have allowed the Jaguars to recoup some of the draft capital from Monday's trades. Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade in October could have served as a blueprint. The Arizona Cardinals received a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick from the Houston Texans in exchange for Harrison—2024's fourth overall pick—and a 2027 sixth-round pick. A 5-4 record didn't seem imaginable when the Rams were the heavy favorites to win Super Bowl LXI before the season started. Injuries have decimated the Rams receiving corps. Davante Adams was put on injured reserve after rupturing a hamstring tendon in Week 6's game against the Cardinals. His estimated recovery time is six to 10 weeks, likely putting his likely return in early December. Puka Nacua suffered a sprained MCL, sprained PCL, and turf toe in his right leg at the end of Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders. He is expected to miss at least a month but has not been put on IR.  
Out of the 26 targets to wide receivers against the Commanders, 19 went to Nacua. The remaining wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster have caught 18 passes for 261 yards with one touchdown this season. Thomas would have been a major short-term upgrade with Adams and Nacua out. He also could have been a younger, lower-cost potential replacement for a soon-to-be 33-year-old Adams, who has an expiring contract. Thomas, who is 24, is under contract in 2027 for a fully guaranteed $2,794,089. A fifth-year option for 2028 could be picked up by May 1 next offseason for around $19.5 million. The big problem is that the Rams wouldn't have had any picks in the first two days of the 2027 NFL Draft if they had acquired Thomas. The 2027 first-round pick was part of the acquisition cost to get reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in June. The 2027 third-round pick was one of four draft choices the Kansas City Chiefs received for cornerback Trent McDuffie in March.  
Restructuring a contract would have been necessary given the Rams' tight salary cap situation to handle Thomas' remaining $537,500 2026 base salary. Quarterback Matthew Stafford would have been a prime candidate since he has 2026's largest cap number at $48,267,348. Tennessee Titans RB Tony Pollard to Green Bay PackersPackers receive: Tony PollardTitans receive: Conditional 2027 fourth-round pick (becomes a third-round pick if Packers advance to Super Bowl LXI and Pollard leads Packers in rushing after trade) Remaining 2026 Salary: $3.61 million Titans 2026 Salary Cap Savings: $3.64 millionPackers 2026 Cap Room: $5.67 millionTitans 2027 Dead Money: None (Expiring Contract)
The Packers are one-dimensional offensively, ranking second in the NFL with 279.7 passing yards per game and last with 68.2 rushing yards per game. Running back Josh Jacobs' broken right ring finger, suffered in Week 9's win over the New England Patriots, required surgery. He could be out for three weeks. Jacobs has been ineffective since coming off the commissioner's exempt list. He missed the first six games of the season on the exempt list while the league was investigating a possible violation of the personal conduct policy related to an alleged domestic violence incident. Jacobs has gained only 80 yards on 36 rushing attempts and scored one touchdown in three games. He is averaging 2.2 yards per carry this year, the lowest average of his career. Pollard would have given Green Bay's running game a boost. He is coming off back-to-back 100-yard rushing games. Pollard is averaging 3.53 yards after contact per carry, according to Pro Football Focus. 
The Packers have plenty of 2027 draft capital, owning 11 picks. This includes four expected compensatory picks. The Packers already have two fourth-round picks. The Titans are going nowhere fast with a 1-7 record. Dealing All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, the franchise's cornerstone, and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks (2027 and 2028) and a 2027 fourth-round pick last week, then safety Amani Hooker and 2027 fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills for a 2027 second-round pick on trade deadline day only increase Tennessee's chances of having the league's worst record and 2027's first-round pick. Pollard is making $7.25 million this year in the final year of a three-year, $21.75 million contract (worth up to $24 million with incentives) signed in 2024 free agency. The $7.25 million consists of a $6.74 million base salary and $510,000 in roster bonuses ($30,000 per active game). There's also $750,000 in incentives that are unlikely to be earned, based primarily on Pollard's statistical achievements. Because Green Bay's bye is in Week 11 and Tennessee's was in Week 9, Pollard would have missed out on $30,000 in per-game roster bonuses, with him able to play a maximum of 16 games this season.
It may not make the most sense for a rebuilding Titans team to re-sign Pollard, who will be 30 in April. The Titans will get a 2028 third-round compensatory pick at best for Pollard if he goes elsewhere in free agency during the offseason.
